page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 96 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in specialized instruction sets and compression tasks. The processor supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to a strong Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 58,987.24. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.41 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 285.51 GB/sec, both placing in the strong performance tier. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the instance achieved a top-tier text generation speed of 386.47 tokens/sec and a strong prompt processing speed of 3,649.93 tokens/sec.

The instance presents a clear tradeoff between compute density and memory capacity. While the 48 dedicated vCPUs deliver strong multi-threaded performance, the 96 GB memory limit restricts its use for memory-intensive datasets. Memory bandwidth tests showed average performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 144.09 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 61.77 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high compute density per resource unit for workloads that leverage its advanced instruction sets, such as cryptography and matrix operations, without requiring massive memory footprints or local storage.

The c4n-highcpu-48 is designed for compute-bound workloads. Appropriate use cases include static web serving, where it demonstrated a strong throughput of 75.61 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a strong Passmark database score of 21,985.02. It is also suitable for lightweight machine learning inference utilizing CPU-based AMX acceleration, cryptography tasks, and multi-threaded data compression pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. It is configured with 96 GB of RAM, a 260 MB L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPUs. The instance demonstrates strong performance in multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and static web serving, alongside top-tier text generation speeds for small-model LLM inference due to built-in AMX and AVX-512 instruction support. However, its 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. Qualitatively, it provides high compute density for CPU-intensive tasks, making it suitable for cryptography, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
